sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content; lexicon = one: tenama (x2), two: bisa (x2). Classification 'Unclassifiable', location not.

sources.note: No phonology content. The only mention (note to Table 1): 'We have not added totally unattested, very poorly attested languages (e.g., Ambermo, attested in two numerals, Fabritius 1855)'. Confirms from the field's own inventory-keeper that no further attestation is known.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1912. Notes on languages in the east of Netherlands New Guinea. Appendix C (pp. 322 ff., with comparative vocabularies) in: Wollaston, A. F. R. 1912. Pygmies & Papuans: The Stone Age To-day in Dutch New Guinea. London: Smith, Elder & Co.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. Wamberan appears only as a name in Ray's list of North-coast languages and as two cells (tenama, bisa; higher numerals blank) in the comparative numeral table, copied from Fabritius 1855. No transcription notes, no accent marks, no prosodic remark.

sources.citation: Fabritius, G. J. 1855. Aanteekeningen omtrent Nieuw-Guinea. Tijdschrift voor Indische Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde IV: 209-215. (Glottolog ref 109606, hh:hw:Fabritius:NNG; the Glottolog's most extensive description and only known attestation of Ambermo)
sources.note: Nothing. The whole Ambermo attestation is one sentence on p. 214: 'Eene stam aan een der takken aan de Ambermo: 1. tenama. 2. bisa. Deze telt alleen met enkel- en meervoud.' -- two numerals, no phonetic or prosodic commentary; p. 215 only locates the Ambermo river east of Geelvink Bay.
Nothing; lists Ambermo among 'Glottolog Unclassifiables without ISO-codes apparently not in ASJP' (no doculect exists).
